title: Your Leadership Role Opens Up New Conversations if You Let It
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This article makes the case that any leadership title, regardless of level, functions as a passport to an external network of peers facing similar challenges. Leaders at comparable levels in other organizations — from front-line supervisors to CEOs — are typically eager to compare notes because they share common problems, and a shared title creates an immediate foundation for connection. The piece argues most leaders underuse this access, missing out on fresh perspectives and approaches that internal colleagues cannot offer. It closes by urging leaders to treat building an external peer network as a deliberate part of the job rather than an occasional nicety.
points: A leadership title grants access to an external network of peers facing similar challenges, regardless of organization size or industry.
Leaders holding comparable roles elsewhere are usually eager to connect and compare notes because of shared challenges.
External relationships provide fresh perspective and different approaches that an internal network cannot match.
The best leaders treat building this external network as a deliberate part of the job, not an occasional extra.
quotes: Smart leaders open doors that many other leaders don’t even realize exist.
The title, authority, and influence any leader enjoys make them interesting to other leaders.
